boundary: Edge of the new lava and pyroclastic land from the 25-hour continuous eruption and lava fountaining of 4-6 Sep 2026 (23:07 WIB 4 Sep to 00:04 WIB 6 Sep). Per Badan Geologi's Sentinel comparison (24 Sep), 32.8 ha were added to the cone's shoreline in the NW-W-SW sector, and two new islets rose ~760 m off the NW coast and ~495 m off the SE coast, on a NW-SE line through the main crater. The rest of the shoreline (N-NE-E) gained no reported land. In NISAR this should be new, decorrelated ground along the W shore plus two isolated spots at sea, against stable older lava on the NE-E side. The whole window is uninhabited (Krakatau islands).

items.title: 32.8 ha of new land on the west shore of Anak Krakatau
items.place: NW-W-SW shoreline of Anak Krakatau island (OSM west coast point)
items.what_it_shows: Badan Geologi (via DW/detik and Antara, 24-25 Sep 2026): Sentinel imagery shows land added to the body of Anak Krakatau in the northwest-west-southwest sector, from pyroclastic deposits and lava flows of the 4-6 Sep continuous eruption, totalling 32.8 ha. Antara Babel quotes the acting head of Badan Geologi saying the 25-hour eruption fed heavy lava flows ('aliran lava deras') that enlarged the volcano.
items.credit: DW Indonesia / detikNews, quoting PVMBG head Rita Susilawati (Badan Geologi)
items.notes: Point is the westernmost vertex of the OSM island outline (relation 20364676), which predates the eruption; the new land lies seaward of it, so the true edge may be a few hundred m further out. Only the sector is published, not a map. Also: https://www.antaranews.com/berita/5757728/ada-daratan-baru-di-dekat-anak-krakatau-ini-penjelasan-ahli. Badan Geologi itself calls this provisional, pending field checks.

items.title: New islet 760 m off the northwest coast
items.place: Sea NW of Anak Krakatau, ~760 m from the NW shore
items.what_it_shows: Badan Geologi (acting head Lana Saria, via Antara, 24 Sep 2026): a new island detected in the northwest sector 760 m from the coast, confirmed by sailors', volunteers' and Sentinel reports as of 23 Sep. It lines up NW-SE with the main crater and the SE islet, and Badan Geologi links it to the 4-6 Sep continuous eruption. A 1 km exclusion radius was set around both islets.
items.credit: M. Riezko Bima Elko Prasetyo / ANTARA, quoting Badan Geologi
items.notes: Computed: 760 m on bearing 315° from the NW-most vertex of the OSM island outline. Only 'NW sector, 760 m from the coast' is published, so the position is uncertain to a few hundred m. Badan Geologi has not decided whether it is a new vent or reworked eruption material. A small isolated target: check whether NISAR resolves it.

items.title: New islet 495 m off the southeast coast
items.place: Sea SE of Anak Krakatau, ~495 m from the SE shore
items.what_it_shows: Same Badan Geologi statement (Antara, 24 Sep 2026): a second new island in the southeast sector, 495 m from the coast, on the NW-SE line through the main crater. Badan Geologi's provisional reading is that fluid magma reached the surface along a NW-SE elongated pathway during the 25-hour eruption.
items.credit: M. Riezko Bima Elko Prasetyo / ANTARA, quoting Badan Geologi
items.notes: Computed: 495 m on bearing 135° from the SE-most vertex of the OSM island outline; position uncertain to a few hundred m. Mechanism quote from DW/detik (24 Sep), link in krakatau-01.

items.title: Lava fountain from the summit crater, 5 September
items.place: Anak Krakatau summit crater (OSM volcano node)
items.what_it_shows: Lampung provincial government photo of the continuous eruption: a lava fountain from Anak Krakatau, seen from the surrounding waters on 5 Sep 2026. Badan Geologi's special report 1512.Lap/GL.03/BGL/2026 describes a continuous red glow resembling a lava fountain that 'produces lava flows', with booms heard from the Pasauran post.
items.credit: Pemprov Lampung (Lampung Provincial Government), via Wikimedia Commons
items.notes: The point is the vent (OSM natural=volcano), not the camera, whose position at sea is unknown. Original source: https://www.lampungprov.go.id/detail-post/aktivitas-erupsi-gunung-anak-krakatau-masih-berlangsung-warga-diminta-waspada-abu-vulkanik. Agency report: https://geologi.esdm.go.id/media-center/fenomena-erupsi-menerus-gunungapi-anak-krakatau-tanggal-5-september-2026. A public-domain satellite alternative is NASA Earth Observatory's Landsat 8 OLI scene of 5 Sep (science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/anak-krakatau-rumbles-again/), which shows the plume, not the flows.

items.title: Northeast shore: no new land
items.place: N-NE shoreline of Anak Krakatau island (OSM NE coast point)
items.what_it_shows: The control. Badan Geologi's Sentinel comparison puts all 32.8 ha of added land in the NW-W-SW sector, so the NE side of the cone gained none. On the north side, the Lava93 (LV93) monitoring station kept sending data through the eruption: its tiltmeter is cited as flat in Badan Geologi's 7 and 11 Sep reports, and its CCTV filmed the fountain at 00:01 WIB on 5 Sep. Its data link was lost only on 16 Sep, after later Strombolian ejecta and ash (and a battery theft found on 27 Sep).
items.licence: Indonesian government agency report; text cited, no image used
items.notes: Point is the NE-most vertex of the OSM island outline, not a surveyed spot. 'No new land here' is inferred from the published sector (NW-W-SW), not from a statement about this shore. LV93's exact site is not published on the pages verified (search snippets say 'north side of the body', unverified), so it is mentioned but not pinned. The LV93 outage report is at https://www.jawapos.com/nasional/2609290478/pencuri-gondol-8-baterai-stasiun-pemantau-anak-krakatau-terobos-area-kawah.
